appraisal_events.evidence: Monsieur a une facilité de parole, une mémoire ! ... comme j'en ai rarement rencontré... Il ferait un excellent prédicateur... deux numéros qui se valent... celui-ci ne damerait pas encore le pion au professeur.
appraisal_events.explanation: Forcheville lavishly praises the peintre's eloquence and memory, ranking him alongside Brichot, but the rambling comparison to a regiment friend who could merely 'dégoiser' for hours about nothing lightly deflates the praise's seriousness.

appraisal_events.evidence: Imputation d'autant plus fausse d'ailleurs que depuis un an Swann n'allait plus guère que chez les Verdurin.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly flags Forcheville's claim about Swann's social habits as false and outdated, quietly undermining his credibility as an accurate, well-informed speaker in the scene.

status_effects.explanation: Forcheville's enthusiastic, if comically overstated, praise mildly elevates the peintre's standing as a witty and eloquent salon speaker.
The narrator's correction exposes Forcheville's assertion about Swann as false and out of date, weakening his credibility as a reliable speaker in front of the group.

ambiguities: Forcheville's praise of the peintre is delivered with a rambling, comic comparison ('dégoiser') that could be read either as genuine (if clumsy) admiration or as the narrator's gentle mockery of Forcheville's own conversational style; a lower-confidence, ironized reading was preferred.

M. Verdurin's anxious sidelong glance at his wife was considered but omitted: it characterizes his vigilance and deference to her moods without a clear evaluative shift landing on him as a distinct local outcome.
